                    ### Question
                    Which of the following characteristics will a patient with helminth infection and one who is responding to an allergen have in common ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. In both patients an increase of cytotoxic T lymphocytes will be detected.
opb. In both patients the innate immunity will be deficient.
opc. In both, an elevated level of serum IgE will be detected.
opd. Both patients have a high risk of developing an autoimmune disease.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Patients with helminth infections and those responding to allergens both exhibit an increased Th2 immune response, which is characterized by elevated levels of serum IgE. This is due to the activation of B cells to produce IgE in response to both helminth antigens and allergens. Therefore, the most accurate statement is that both conditions involve elevated serum IgE levels. While there may be some immune modulation in both cases, it does not necessarily imply a deficiency in innate immunity. Additionally, the risk of developing autoimmune diseases is not a common characteristic of either condition. Thus, the correct option is that both patients will have elevated serum IgE levels.
